description: Clear all fragment information. All fragment data is destroyed, event tracking is stopped, and the fragment IDs held in all bodies (balls and clumps) are reset to 0. This is a complete reset of the fragment tracking system.
notes: Destructive operation - all fragment information is permanently lost
All fragment IDs in balls and clumps are reset to 0
Fragment event tracking is stopped (if it was active)
Does NOT disable fragment auto-computation - use fragment deactivate for that
Does NOT affect fragment persistence settings in contacts (pb_persist remains unchanged)
After clearing, can recompute fragments with fragment compute or fragment activate
Useful for resetting fragment analysis between simulation phases
No parameters required - clears all fragments globally
Related commands: fragment activate, fragment deactivate, fragment compute, fragment list, fragment register
Resets every fragment ID to 0 and erases the history; the auto-computation state is left as it was. Not undoable.
No direct Python SDK method for fragment clear
Must use command interface: itasca.command('fragment clear')
After clearing, can verify with Python: ball.fragment() should return 0
Fragment clearing is a global operation, not object-specific

command_vs_python.python:
itasca.command('fragment clear')
# Verify: ball.fragment() returns 0 for all balls

examples.description: Clear all fragment information and reset all fragment IDs to 0. Use case: Reset fragment tracking between simulation phases.

examples.command:
fragment activate cycles 100
model cycle 5000
fragment clear
fragment activate cycles 100
examples.description: Track fragments, clear data, restart tracking fresh. Use case: Analyze fragments in different simulation phases independently.
Clear old fragment data, then compute fresh fragment IDs. Use case: Get clean snapshot of current fragment state.
Stop auto-computation, then clear all fragment data. Use case: Complete cleanup of fragment tracking system.

examples.command:
model solve
fragment compute
ball list range group-slot 'frag' 1
fragment clear
model cycle 1000
fragment compute
